name: Mitch McConnell
role: US senator from Kentucky (1985-2027); Senate Republican leader (2007-2025)
summary: McConnell is a Republican senator known for low taxes, judicial confirmations, opposition to the Affordable Care Act and to campaign finance limits, and a strong national defense. He backed NATO and Ukraine aid and argued against isolationism, and in 2025 opposed broad tariffs. He voted to acquit Trump in 2021 on jurisdictional grounds while holding him morally responsible for January 6.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Voted against final passage of the Affordable Care Act on 24 December 2009 and for amendments to strip its new entitlement programs; votes alone, and his criticism of Medicare for All was found only on Wikipedia, so -1 medium.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: As Senate Republican leader he led a party-line block of a minimum wage increase in April 2014.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: His record is consistently against higher taxes on the wealthy: he led the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, introduced a 2019 bill to abolish the estate tax and voted for the 2025 reconciliation bill. On July 1, 2025 he did vote Yea on a motion to waive the budget point of order against Collins Amdt. 2812, which applied a 39.6 percent top rate and also added rural health funding; that motion failed 22-78. One procedural vote on a mixed amendment, with no statement from him, does not show he wants significantly higher taxes on the wealthy, but it keeps him from the strongest answer.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Voted in 2002 to permanently repeal the estate tax and against motions to keep it with a higher exemption, and in 2001 against amendments preserving it for the largest estates; a consistent voting record, so medium.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Led passage of the 2018 regulatory relief law and opposed Paycheck Fairness Act as a gift to trial lawyers; record favours lighter regulation.

limit-guns.rationale: Voted Nay on the 2013 Manchin-Toomey background-check amendment (S.Amdt. 715), yet voted Yea on the 2022 Bipartisan Safer Communities Act (cloture and passage); mixed record favours modest measures, not strict limits.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Said after Obergefell that he opposed same-sex marriage but that it was the law of the land; voted Nay on the 2022 Respect for Marriage Act (H.R. 8404 passage).

abortion-legal.rationale: Describes himself as anti-abortion, has voted for many anti-abortion bills and called the 2022 Dobbs decision courageous and correct.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Re-sourcing under rules 3: the earlier answer cited only Wikipedia, and the underlying statement was not found in this pass, so no known position.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Voted for the Protect America Act of 2007 (S. 1927, passed 60-28), which authorised acquiring foreign intelligence without individual warrants; a vote, so medium.

empower-police-military.rationale: Consistently urged sustained defense investment and rebuilding the defense industrial base; the statement's police component is not documented.

free-trade.rationale: Supported free trade and urged preserving NAFTA in 2018; warned that nobody wins a trade war; voted in 2025 to end tariff emergencies.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Voted Yea in 2025 on Senate resolutions ending the emergencies behind tariffs on Canada (April and October), Brazil and global tariffs (October); in 2018 warned that nobody wins a trade war.

nation-first.rationale: In his July 2024 remarks he told isolationists that American leadership is indispensable, that US credibility is not divisible, and that European security is tied to America's own.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Called climate mitigation the most expensive attack on jobs, urged governors not to comply with the Clean Power Plan, and criticised the Green New Deal.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Sponsored the 2008 Gas Price Reduction Act for more domestic drilling and made Keystone XL approval a first Senate priority in 2014.

military-superiority.rationale: Argues that US promises and threats must be backed by hard power under peace through strength.

collective-defense.rationale: Said NATO's success is premised on collective defense.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Defends NATO and the American-led order; introduced a 2019 amendment warning against precipitous troop withdrawals from Syria and Afghanistan.

non-intervention.rationale: Supported the 2017 Syria strike, backed Ukraine aid and sanctions, and in 2025 backed military action against Iran.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Voted for the 2002 joint resolution authorising force against Iraq (77-23), a war not fought in response to an attack on the United States.

multipolar-world.rationale: Frames the American-led order as the basis of security and urges the West to back it with hard power.

corporate-influence.rationale: Led opposition to McCain-Feingold, lead plaintiff in McConnell v. FEC and a key opponent of donor-disclosure rules; has not treated campaign money as excessive influence.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Voted in 2011 for S.J.Res. 10, a constitutional balanced budget amendment, the most binding fiscal rule available; a vote, so medium.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Re-sourcing under rules 3: the earlier answer cited only Wikipedia, and the underlying statement was not found in this pass, so no known position.

voter-id.rationale: Re-sourcing under rules 3: the earlier answer cited only Wikipedia, and the underlying statement was not found in this pass, so no known position.

strong-leader.rationale: Opposed ending the legislative filibuster (2019) and said in 2021 the Senate should not grab power the Constitution does not give it.

separated-powers.rationale: In his 2021 remarks praised the framers' firewall and constitutional limits on Senate authority.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

rehabilitation.rationale: Brought the First Step Act, which expands recidivism-reduction programming in federal prisons, to the floor and voted for it (87-12) in December 2018; no stated view on rehabilitation versus punishment was found, and his law-and-order rhetoric elsewhere keeps this low.

expand-nuclear.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

state-directs-investment.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

one-party-rule.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

democracy-best.rationale: In his January 6, 2021 certification speech he argued Congress should not overrule the voters even though he disagreed with the outcome, and urged accepting defeat; this is about accepting an election result, not a general claim that democracy is the best form of government.

profit-exploitation.rationale: 2012 address: rejected equating profit with cheating customers or mistreating employees.

consent-of-governed.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Voted for the 1993 Religious Freedom Restoration Act (97-3), which lets people claim exemption from general laws that substantially burden their religious exercise, and voted against an amendment excluding prisoners from it.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: In his January 6, 2021 speech he warned that overturning the result would end the Electoral College, which he said most Republicans had been defending for years.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Said former presidents remain subject to criminal and civil law.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: He was lead plaintiff in McConnell v. FEC, asking the Supreme Court to strike down provisions of the 2002 campaign finance law Congress had passed, so he holds that courts may constrain elected majorities.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Defended the First Amendment as an inviolable limit on legislative action.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: In a 2024 op-ed he criticised Biden's block of Nippon Steel's purchase of U.S. Steel as unjustified for a close ally, while citing the Exon-Florio review framework with careful limits; this is one case and he accepts review where national security is truly threatened.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Voted in 1986 for the $100 million package of military and other aid to the Nicaraguan Contras fighting the Sandinista government, and against substitutes barring aid to paramilitary groups in Nicaragua; votes alone, so medium.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Condemned government intimidation of dissenting political organizations.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Favored allied coordination against Russia, China, Iran and North Korea.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The Heller amicus brief he signed defends the right of law-abiding persons to keep usable firearms for lawful self-defense in the home, which treats armed self-defense as legitimate.

pollution-taxes.rationale: A 2024 Senate floor speech warned of the economic effects of a carbon tax in describing House bills, while also attacking EPA regulation and green subsidies; the evidence is a single passing line on one kind of pollution tax.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Signed the 2008 congressional amicus brief in Heller arguing that the Second Amendment protects individuals unaffiliated with any militia in keeping firearms at home; a signed brief, not his own speech, so medium.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Opposed cancellation as an unfair transfer to higher-earning graduates.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: He condemned the D.C. Council measure eliminating almost all mandatory minimum sentences; this is rhetoric about one local law, not a stated general view on fixed sentences for repeat offenders.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Mixed record: in 1991 he voted for a resolution urging an international criminal court or tribunal to try Saddam Hussein, but he voted in 2001 to shield US personnel from ICC prosecution and in 2025 for cloture on a bill sanctioning the ICC for pursuing US or allied officials.

notes:
Living person: answers are limited to votes, sponsored bills and his own statements; everything else is null. Early in his career he reportedly held more moderate views on abortion and public unions; his mature position is used. Position on tariffs is from 2025 and reverses nothing earlier. Speeches s3-s5 and Senate vote records s6-s7 were downloaded as raw text/XML and checked directly; Wikipedia pages were read through a summarising fetch tool. Searches for full floor texts on campaign finance, the filibuster and hemp did not surface usable pages, so those positions stay unrecorded or rest on Wikipedia.

Merged with an independent gpt-6.1-sol audit: 17 answers taken from it, 15 agreed, 1 conflicts settled by the integrator.

gpt-6.1-sol notes: Independent pass. Prior answers not read. Downloaded full 2012 First Amendment address, January 6 and impeachment speeches, 2025 interview, 22 indexed Senate releases, 2026 Congressional Record texts and official roll calls. Government-page release IDs worked when direct permalink downloads did not. Votes alone are medium at most. The July 2025 vote for a 39.6% ultra-high-income rate is retained alongside tax-cut votes, not ignored. Do not attribute neighbouring Congressional Record speakers’ AI and energy remarks to McConnell: the March 12, 2026 speech attributed to him concerns Iran and Ukraine. Vaccines and military space investment do not establish views on technology solving most problems or civilian space expansion. Support for modest gun legislation does not by itself settle strictly limited ownership; that item remains null. Hemp is not all recreational drugs; education decisions are not general subsidiarity. Social protection during emergencies is not a position on all welfare dependency. Nine of the ten priority theories remain unknown; profit-exploitation is answered from his own explicit rejection of profit implying employee abuse. Reviewed every remaining null against the full statement list. Condemnation of January 6 alone does not establish an exceptionless rule against every form of political violence; that statement remains null.

claude-opus-5-5 deepening pass (2026-10-31) on lines 12, 13 and 14: searched the Voteview roll calls (RFRA, First Step Act, ICC, New START, Contra aid, Syria train-and-equip), the 2008 Heller congressional amicus brief, McConnell v. FEC, his Electoral College remarks and ICC statements. Eight answers added. The 2024 letter threatening ICC sanctions was found only in press reports, and his court-packing floor remarks and the statement answering Governor Beshear on the Electoral College were blocked (403), so they are not cited. New START votes and the 2014 Syria CR vote were left out as nearby cases (one treaty is not arms reduction in general; the CR covered much else). Rules 3 re-sourcing: universal-healthcare (-2 high to -1 medium), surveillance-ok (2 high to 1 medium), tax-inheritance (high to medium), defensive-wars-only and fiscal-rules-binding (2 high to 2 medium) now rest on Voteview roll calls; legalize-drugs, voter-id and avoid-deficit-stimulus rested only on Wikipedia and are now null.
